feedback: This candidate changes one field from the iteration 3 design (score 724.5, the best raced so far): kp 4.5 to 5.0. Sensor geometry, weights, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, base_speed 1.1 and line_loss are unchanged, so the effect of the gain change is isolated. All values are inside the contract ranges. Iteration 3 showed the oval (20/20, 2.14 s) and s-bend (20/20, 2.30 s) finishing comfortably under 3 s. The slalom is the bottleneck: 19 of 20 trials ended off_track at mean progress 0.67, with control_effort 15.2 and steering_oscillation 0.33. That points to limited steering authority on the sharp alternating bends, since sensor y is already at its contract maximum of 0.08. Raising kp is the next step that the evidence supports, and it is a small step. I cannot state how it will perform. Read the race as follows. If the slalom completes more often or progress rises above 0.8, keep kp near 5.0 and consider a small base_speed reduction only if the slalom still exits at low progress. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4, raise kd slightly (for example 1.0 to 1.2) rather than lowering kp, because iteration 3 shows kd helped damp the faster corrections. If the oval or s-bend stops finishing, or the oval completion_time moves toward 2.5 s or more, return kp toward 4.5 before changing speed. Watch max_error and line_loss_events on the slalom to see whether recovery improves.
requested_changes: If the slalom still ends off_track with progress below 0.8 and max_error near 0.06, try base_speed 1.0 with kp 5.0 kept, because iteration 3 slalom progress of 0.67 at speed 1.1 suggests the bends are taken too fast.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 with kp 5.0 (iteration 3 value 0.33), raise kd from 1.0 to 1.2 before lowering kp, since kd 0.8 to 1.0 in iterations 2 to 3 came with better slalom and s-bend results.
If the oval or s-bend stops finishing or the oval completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, return kp to 4.5, the iteration 3 value that finished 20/20 on both tracks.
